Flamboyant

/flam-BOY-unt/ — rhymes with buoyant · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is flamboyant behaves, dresses, or performs in a bold, colorful, and attention-grabbing way.

The skater's flamboyant sequined costume sparkled from every corner of the rink.

Worked Example

A performer takes the stage in a sequined jacket that catches the light, towering boots with buckles, and hair dyed electric blue, moving with exaggerated gestures to command the crowd's attention.

Flamboyant captures not just 'bold' or 'showy' but a specific blend of personal style, boldness, and attention-grabbing performance—that deliberate, dazzling self-expression is what makes flamboyant more precise than simpler words.

How Flamboyant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

showy

showy: designed to attract notice and admiration

theatrical

theatrical: dramatic and exaggerated, as if performing

expressive

expressive: clearly showing feelings and lively personality

Antonyms

reserved

reserved: holding back, quiet in manner and style

subdued

subdued: toned down, soft, not attention-grabbing

How Strong Is It? — quiet → expressive → bold → flamboyant

quiet vs. flamboyant

quiet vs. flamboyant: Quiet is the opposite pole from flamboyant: a quiet dresser avoids notice, while a flamboyant one demands it.

expressive vs. flamboyant

expressive vs. flamboyant: Expressive is far gentler than flamboyant; an expressive performer shows feeling clearly, but a flamboyant one turns every gesture into a dazzling show.

bold vs. flamboyant

bold vs. flamboyant: Bold comes close, but flamboyant goes further: a bold outfit makes a statement, while a flamboyant one adds glitter, color, and theater until no one can look away.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of flamboyant.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — flamb

Root — flamb: flame, blaze (French (from Latin flamma))

Suffix — -ant

Suffix — -ant: doing or showing (adjective-forming) (French/Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Flamb- means 'flame' and -ant makes it an adjective, so flamboyant literally means 'flaming' — a flamboyant person blazes with bold color and energy, grabbing attention like a flickering fire.

Use the root in a new word: flammable

Use the root in a new word: flammable: Something flammable catches fire easily, and a flamboyant style 'flames' too — it comes from the same flame root and blazes boldly enough to catch every eye.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / informal

Use flamboyant when someone's personality, style, or performance is deliberately bold, colorful, and attention-grabbing. For just 'showy' or 'visible,' simpler words work better.
